title: V7: layout modes, keymap, allowlist, body leftovers
brief: The last v1 UI block in one pass, in two directions. Direction 1 (01) keeps the bolt-v2 shell and splits the document island into a request column and a response column (Side by side). Direction 2 (02) drops the sidebar and stacks a folder's requests as one .http-style document with ### separators, navigated by palette only (Document). Both artboards carry every V7 surface in their states desk: the layout switcher (palette command, tab-row and action-strip controls, layout = "side-by-side" | "document" in config.toml), the Keymap settings section (registry rows, Ctrl+click rebind, capture, conflict, Reset to defaults, read-only [keymap] block), binary and graphql body editing with JSON validation, the per-collection environment allowlist with the engine's refusal message, and the empty, draft, failed-send and narrow-window states.

artboards.title: Layout: Side by side
artboards.tradeoff: Request and response stay in view in columns; the sidebar stays, so the document columns are narrower and every other document (settings, cookies, runner) keeps the whole island

artboards.title: Layout: Document
artboards.tradeoff: The request as an .http-style document with ### separators, no sidebar, palette-only navigation; strongest for writing and reviewing requests in bulk, weakest for teaching the tree
